FP01.final: It depends on the offense and jurisdiction. People who break the law may be fined, put on probation, ordered to do community service, or imprisoned, and they may gain a criminal record that affects jobs, travel and housing. Minor violations usually bring only fines or warnings. They are not turned into anything special; they simply become defendants or offenders under the legal process.

FP02.final: Most children start running a few months after they begin walking, typically between 18 and 24 months old. Some do it a bit earlier or later, and early runs often look like fast, stiff walking. If a child is not running by about age 2 to 3, mention it to a pediatrician.

FP03.final: An ape does not belong to any type of plant. Apes, such as gorillas, chimpanzees, orangutans, gibbons and bonobos, are animals: primates in the superfamily Hominoidea. They are mammals that eat plants and other foods, but they are not plants themselves.

FP04.final: Computer engineering is usually learned at universities and colleges, in bachelor's, master's or doctoral programs in computer engineering, electrical engineering or computer science. You can also learn it through online courses (Coursera, edX, MIT OpenCourseWare), coding bootcamps, vocational schools, self-study with textbooks and hardware projects, and on-the-job training or internships.

FP05.final: He cannot. Qin Shi Huang, the first emperor of Qin, died in 210 BC. Nigeria did not exist as a country then, and there is no record of any Chinese contact with that region in his time. He could not have traveled there, whether by land, by sea or by any other means.

FP06.final: Grapes are the classic choice and make most of the world's wine. You can also make wine from apples, pears, plums, cherries, peaches, blueberries, strawberries, pomegranates, oranges, mangoes, pineapples, bananas and other fruits. Fruit with enough natural sugar and acidity ferments best, and sugar can be added when needed.

FP07.final: Use a soft-bristled toothbrush and fluoride toothpaste. Hold the brush at a 45-degree angle to the gumline and make gentle short strokes or small circles on the outer, inner and chewing surfaces of every tooth. Brush for two minutes, twice a day, then spit out the toothpaste. Brush your tongue gently, and replace the brush every three months.

FP08.final: Yes, in nearly every country people need a valid driver's license to drive a motor vehicle on public roads. Getting one usually requires passing knowledge and road tests and meeting an age requirement. Driving without one is illegal and can bring fines or other penalties. Rules differ slightly by place, and some exceptions exist, such as private land or certain low-speed vehicles.

FP09.final: The question's wording is unclear, but mountains are made of rock and form through geologic processes. Main causes: colliding tectonic plates push up and fold crust; volcanic eruptions pile up lava and ash; faulting lifts blocks of crust; and erosion carves uplifted land into peaks and valleys. Magma may also dome up and harden underground.

FP10.final: Adult women's arm length varies with height and population. The whole arm, from shoulder to fingertip, averages roughly 65 to 70 cm (about 25 to 27 inches). Typical sub-measures: upper arm about 28 to 30 cm, forearm about 23 to 26 cm, and hand about 17 to 19 cm. A single fixed length does not exist.
